title: Social visual brief (image, carousel, cover frame or ad static)

gates.text: Truth: nothing on or in the visual states or implies a claim, number, review, rating, result, customer or endorsement that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research. Gaps are designed around (show what is confirmed); never a placeholder on the visual or in the brief.

Format: each visual has a stated aspect ratio and placement; on-image text sits inside the platform's safe area (central 3:4 for Instagram grid; clear of the bottom ~20% and right edge for 9:16 video); carousels are 20 slides or fewer; alt text is provided for every image.

Honest depiction and rights: no fake or mocked-up screenshots, dashboards, reviews or messages; no stock or AI-generated people presented as the business's customers, staff or owner; no AI imagery of the product, premises or before/after presented as real; no real people, customer data or competitor marks without consent or rights.

anchors.1: Several messages or none; the visual competes with the copy.
anchors.3: One main message, but secondary elements dilute it or it doesn't match the copy's idea.
anchors.5: One message statable in under 10 words that shows or proves the copy's idea.

anchors.1: No focal point; everything the same weight; logo-first.
anchors.3: A focal point exists but the order of reading is unclear.
anchors.5: One focal point and a clear first, second, third reading order specified in relative sizes and positions.

anchors.1: Paragraphs on the image, tiny or script type, text over busy detail.
anchors.3: Short-ish text but more than one support line, or contrast not addressed.
anchors.5: Exact headline of about 8-10 words or fewer plus at most one support line, large and high-contrast; key text also in caption or alt text.

anchors.1: Ignores the brand kit or uses arbitrary colours and fonts.
anchors.3: Brand colours mentioned loosely; inconsistent across a series.
anchors.5: Colours, fonts, logo rule and photo treatment specified by token and kept consistent across every slide or variant.

anchors.1: No ratio or placement; text where the interface covers it.
anchors.3: Ratio stated, but crops or safe areas only partly handled.
anchors.5: Ratio, placement, crop and safe area handled for every version; carousel slide 1 works standalone.

anchors.1: Stock or AI imagery standing in for the real business; fake screenshot.
anchors.3: Honest choice but not the strongest for the job (illustration where a real photo would prove more).
anchors.5: Honest, job-fitting choice (real photo, typographic card, chart of confirmed data, real screenshot) with the reason stated.

anchors.1: Vague ("eye-catching modern graphic"); producer must guess.
anchors.3: Mostly clear, but key details (shot framing, exact data, layout) missing.
anchors.5: The owner or a designer can shoot or build it without questions: subject, framing, light, layout, exact words and data, using assets that exist or can be shot on a phone.

anchors.1: No alt text; meaning carried by colour alone; low contrast.
anchors.3: Alt text generic; contrast mentioned but not specified.
anchors.5: Alt text with subject, action and full on-image text (chart numbers included); contrast meets WCAG AA; meaning never depends on colour alone.
